acceptance: Installs as an actual app on the target platform
Works locally without the discontinued production servers
Player can drive and drift in a solo race
Player can race against functioning AI opponents
Evidence of actual interactive gameplay, not just a splash screen or static asset view
Original gameplay, art, sound, physics and controls retained; no substitute kart simulator
Both speed and item races run locally with multiple AI, working laps, finish and results
Item races include functioning original items; no online multiplayer mode
Original lobby, character selection and garage/car selection flow retained with local profile and inventory data
Original menu navigation and race entry/return flow; diagnostic direct-map menu is only an intermediate test tool

Original launch-to-lobby, character/garage navigation, equipment selection, race setup, start, results and return-to-lobby interaction flow retained; server-dependent profile changes are handled locally
Local profile and selected equipment persist between app launches

Offline content fully unlocked locally: all retained characters, karts, cosmetics, parts and tracks are available without purchase, progression or server entitlement checks; missing asset files must be identified separately
intermediate_milestone: Load the retained iOS training map and establish local player control
preservation: Keep original installed app and data; modify and test an independent copy
status: Original Drift 2.71.1, tested on an iPad running iPadOS 16.1: Village_I01 speed and item races each run with one local player and three original AI. All three AI finish with original checkpoints, ranking, podium and final results. The unattended player retires; a full player-driven finish remains unverified. Original table initialization restores 79 tables and 25 item cubes. AI pickup and original Shield/Waterbomb objects linked to AI components are observed; complete per-item hit/defense/effect coverage remains unverified. Simultaneous real touchscreen steering and drift update original input fields and release correctly; complete drift handling, camera and screenshot orientation need further checks. Local replay through original relative map travel is verified with a second complete AI item race in the same process. A diagnostic native selector now queues original speed/item travel on the original game thread; After switching from item to speed in the same iOS process, three original AI finish with original EndGame/results at 50.144/53.885/54.922 seconds. This selector is intermediate only. A usable original pause flow remains missing. The original ARM64 iOS app also runs as a separately signed Mac Catalyst diagnostic copy: Village_I01 item races and original final results are visibly verified, in an App Sandbox with no network entitlement. Mac player controls and window resizing remain unverified. A clean Mac diagnostic rebuild and deep signature validation pass. Actual iPhone play, offline Android play and an original 2004-PC-client port remain unverified. The original lobby probe creates the original debug account only in local worlds and selects the retained mobile UI. The earlier Mac probe visibly showed the original lobby, garage category screen, empty kart inventory page and settings; the original settings return flow works. Thirteen lobby levels are loaded. The updated iPad build also visibly shows the original mobile lobby, settings page and mode cards, with thirteen lobby levels loaded. The experimental original-inventory initializer now reads the retained original initial table and calls original inventory/equipment functions on the original game thread. Mac read-only inspection confirms 96 initial items, 16 equipped slots and a null NetDriver; the updated iPad records the same initialization counts and visibly displays the original character and kart. Garage equipment updates, persistent saves and original race entry/return remain incomplete. An optional local-catalog grant now applies all 3,326 original item definitions to the original local inventory. Mac read-only verification confirms all six populated original inventory categories total 3,326 items. Two updated iPad launches record the full catalog grant and return to the original lobby. A clean Mac build includes all 26 retained downloaded resource chunks plus the original app resources. This does not verify every asset, garage equipment operation or track unlock. Full unlocked-content acceptance remains incomplete. No complete deliverable is claimed.

implementation.source: Reverse engineer and modify the preserved original client; do not substitute a newly written kart game. Write our analysis and patch tooling ourselves.
implementation.allowed_research: Study publicly described principles and validate behavior; implement our own code
implementation.platform_dependencies: Native operating-system SDKs, compilers and standard libraries
implementation.original_assets: Import retained original art and sound separately; do not publish original game assets as our source code
implementation.runtime: Original app executable, original engine, assets, physics, sound and gameplay. Offline startup and local AI race patches are the work to be completed.
